levels.name: First Ripple
levels.hint: Everything here spread from one point. Walk there (click, or WASD), press Space to plant, step off the seed, then Grow. Living ground overgrows whatever stands on it.
levels.tip: The shape is symmetric. Its centre is where it began.
levels.intro: You wake on cold ground with a lantern in your hand and no memory of lighting it. Around you lies the shape of something that once spread. It had a beginning. Find it.
levels.outro: The ground remembers. Where you planted the seed, it grew back exactly as it had.

levels.name: Against the Wall
levels.hint: Rock never changes, blocks your way, and nothing grows through it. Read the shape of what got past.
levels.tip: The wall and the left edge clip the ripple, but its top and bottom are still symmetric: the origin is level with the gap.
levels.intro: Someone raised walls here, long ago, to keep the ripples in. The walls outlasted them.
levels.outro: Stone does not grow. That is why it is still here.

levels.name: Two Springs
levels.hint: Two beginnings. Where the ripples met, the shape tells you where they started.
levels.tip: Each ripple alone is the shape from the first level. Find two such centres.
levels.intro: Two beginnings, one ending. Whatever lived here met in the middle and became a single thing.
levels.outro: Two seeds, one shape. Nothing that meets stays separate.

levels.name: Spark
levels.hint: A different law now. Each cell lives for one generation and only lonely neighbours light up. Explore: the rings are out there.
levels.tip: The four rings sit two cells diagonally from where the spark was. The spark cell itself is empty now.
levels.intro: The law changes underfoot. Here nothing lived past its first breath, and only the lonely were born.
levels.outro: A spark leaves rings. The spark itself is gone.

levels.name: Ember
levels.hint: Rock does not grow and does not count. The wall ate part of one ring.
levels.tip: Three rings are whole and the wall bit the fourth. The origin is the centre of all four.
levels.intro: A ring bitten by stone. Even sparks obey walls.
levels.outro: The wall took its share and kept it.

levels.name: Twin Sparks
levels.hint: Two sparks. Where their rings would overlap, the cells had too many neighbours to be born. An ember drifts along the row below them: cross once it has passed.
levels.tip: Two sparks, six cells apart. The rings that would have touched lost their touching columns.
levels.intro: Two sparks, close enough to touch. Where they would have met, nothing was born at all. And something still moves down here: an ember of the old growth, drifting along its row. It burns what it touches.
levels.outro: Too many neighbours and the birth does not happen. Loneliness was the law.

levels.name: Echo
levels.hint: A parity law: alive next turn if the neighbour count is odd. One origin echoes outward.
levels.tip: The origin sits at the middle of the small cross in the centre.
levels.intro: Deeper in, the law is stranger: a cell lives when its neighbours are odd in number. What lived here echoed.
levels.outro: An echo is the shape of its source, repeated and thinned.

levels.name: Interference
levels.hint: Under this law two origins add like waves. Where both echoes land, they cancel out.
levels.tip: Two echoes, four cells apart. The centre column is where they cancelled each other out.
levels.intro: Two echoes crossed here. Where both arrived they cancelled, as waves do.
levels.outro: Where two things agree completely they leave nothing. You are learning the grammar.

levels.name: Coral
levels.hint: Here nothing dies: every cell that is born stays. The rocks carved the shape.
levels.tip: Nothing dies here, so the origin is still alive: it is the very heart of the coral.
levels.intro: Here nothing dies. Everything ever born is still here, packed against the rocks that shaped it.
levels.outro: The origin is still alive at the heart of it. Some things keep their beginning.

levels.name: Headwaters
levels.hint: Two springs, one river, two fords. Trace each flood back to where it started.
levels.tip: Each spring is the first ripple grown for five generations. Find both centres; the river only clips the edges.
levels.intro: A river of stone with two fords. On each side, a spring that flooded for five generations.
levels.outro: Rivers clip what they cannot stop. The springs still tell where they rose.

levels.name: Trinity
levels.hint: Three sparks this time. Where ring sets meet, the touching cells were never born.
levels.tip: Each ring set is centred two cells diagonally from its spark. Two sparks sit on one row, the third below them.
levels.intro: Three sparks. You have seen two touch; now three, and the silence between them is louder.
levels.outro: Every ring is centred on a spark that is no longer there.

levels.name: Fracture
levels.hint: Rock cuts through this echo. Rock is never alive and never counts as a neighbour.
levels.tip: The echo would be symmetric without the seam. Mirror the intact half to find the centre.
levels.intro: A seam of stone runs through an echo. Half of it is missing. Half is enough.
levels.outro: Mirror what survived and the lost half reappears.

levels.name: Tide Pools
levels.hint: Two corals, and nothing dies. Where they grew into each other the shape is denser.
levels.tip: Each origin is still alive at the heart of its own coral, six cells apart on one row.
levels.intro: Two corals grew into each other around a pair of rocks. Nothing here has ever died.
levels.outro: Their hearts still beat, six cells apart.

levels.name: Lattice
levels.hint: One origin, five generations of echo. The pattern repeats itself at every scale.
levels.tip: Nine rings in a three-by-three lattice: the origin is the centre of the central ring.
levels.intro: One origin, five generations of echo, nine rings. The world repeating itself at every scale.
levels.outro: The centre of the centre. You are close now.

levels.name: Confluence
levels.hint: Three springs. A wall with one gap divides them, and every ripple keeps what it makes.
levels.tip: Two springs above the wall, one below it. The one below leaked up through the gap.
levels.intro: Three springs behind a broken wall. This is the last ruin, and the shape in it is one you know: it is the shape you woke inside.
levels.outro: You planted the seeds where the springs rose, and the world grew back around you. It began here. So did you.

levels.name: The Cistern
levels.hint: You woke without a seed. One lies in the dark behind the wall. Find it, then find where the ripple began.
levels.tip: The pocket in the corner has one way in, on its right side. The ripple's centre is the middle of its symmetric shape.
levels.intro: Past the last ruin you thought was last, the ground goes on. This time you wake empty-handed. Whatever was planted here was carried in from somewhere else.
levels.outro: A seed is a thing you carry before it is a thing you plant.

levels.name: Two Lanterns
levels.hint: Two sparks lit this. Two seeds lie in the corners, one each side, and an ember paces each pocket. Each wall has a single gap.
levels.tip: Each set of rings is centred two cells diagonally from its spark, and the two sparks share a row.
levels.intro: Two seeds this time, and they are not together. Whoever carried them came from both ends of the world.
levels.outro: You carried what they carried, and stood where they stood.

levels.name: Choir Stalls
levels.hint: The seed lies along this bottom row. The echo rose beyond the long wall, which is open at both ends.
levels.tip: The origin sits in the middle of the small cross at the echo's centre.
levels.intro: A long wall with the echo behind it and the seed before it. The wall is open at both ends, as walls that outlast their makers tend to be.
levels.outro: Odd numbers make the choir. The centre holds the note.

levels.name: Reef Walk
levels.hint: Two corals, two seeds lying in the far corners. The wall between has a gap at each end.
levels.tip: Nothing dies under this law, so each origin is still alive at the heart of its coral, eight cells apart.
levels.intro: The corals here grew towards each other and never quite met. The seeds that started them were left where the reef ends.
levels.outro: What never dies still needs to have begun.

levels.name: Lantern's End
levels.hint: Three seeds lie along the bottom of the world, beyond a wall broken in two places, with embers pacing the row before them. Three springs rose above.
levels.tip: Two springs high on the left and right, one lower in the middle. The wall clipped the lowest one.
levels.intro: The last of the ground. Three seeds wait below a broken wall, and above it the largest shape you have seen. You already know whose it is.
levels.outro: Three springs, three seeds, one wanderer. The lantern goes out because it is no longer needed.
